Name: AB-MCTS
Title: Scaling LLM Inference-Time Compute with Adaptive Branching Tree Search
Experiment: Starting from a single root node, we perform nnodes iterations, each adding one new node, resulting in a total of 1 + nnodes nodes. Each iteration has three steps: (1) Selection, where we select a node N for expansion; (2) Expansion, where we expand N by generating a new answer from node N, creating a new child node Nnew and appending it to N. Specifically, if N is the root, the new answer is directly generated from the task prompt; if N is non-root, the new answer refines the answer associated with N, using external feedback; and (3) Score backup, where we propagate the score of Nnew up toward the root of the tree T. We adopt different backup rules in our proposed methods (see Section 3.3 and 3.4). In our setting, no separate rollout is needed, since each node’s score r can be evaluated directly once an output is generated. After nnodes iterations, we select the best node based on a chosen criterion.

Name: Curiosity Learning
Title: Tree Search Based on Curiosity Learning
Experiment: Prepare a separate model to predict outcome for each node. Curiosity reward is calculated on the difference of predicted and actual outcomes. Apply algorithm taking balance between exploitation (basic reward) and exploration (curiosity reward).

Name: DAG Searching
Title: Merging Nodes: Combining Ideas
Experiment: Introduce a merge action to combine ideas & results of two nodes.

Name: cost_aware_portfolio_mcts
Title: Cost-Aware Portfolio Search: Online Model Selection in LLM Tree Exploration
Experiment: 1) Define PORTFOLIO = [("gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14",0.9),("gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14",0.3),("gpt-4.1-small-2025-04-14",0.3)]. 2) Extend generate_fn(state, task, ...) with parameter cost_penalty_coeff λ; after call_llm compute reward = public_score - λ*cost, return (state, reward). 3) In main(), keep a global total_cost; set a budget B (e.g. $20) and update λ = max(0, total_cost/B). 4) Build generate_fns dict: for each (model,temp) create partial(generate_fn, model_name=model, model_temp=temp, cost_penalty_coeff=lambda), key name e.g. "nano_0.9". 5) Run StandardMCTS and AB-MCTS with max_num_nodes=16 under baseline (single model) and portfolio conditions, record private accuracy, total_cost, solved-per-dollar. 6) Expectation: portfolio search yields higher accuracy within the same budget, demonstrating adaptive cost/quality trade-offs.

Name: overfit_guard
Title: Static-and-Dynamic Over-fit Detection to Improve Generalisation in LLM Tree Search
Experiment: Add utils/overfit_guard.py implementing detect_overfit(code, demos) -> risk in [0,1]. Static heuristics: (a) literal demo grids or substrings, (b) nested numeric lists >15 numbers, (c) 'if input ==' string matches, (d) returns of constant grid size. Dynamic check: create a lightly perturbed demo input (e.g. rotate or shuffle) and exec transform; if output unchanged or identical to any demo output mark risk=1. In experiment.generate_fn(), after obtaining pycode and raw_score, compute risk and adjust score: if guard_mode=='off' keep raw_score; if 'soft' use raw_score - alpha*risk; if 'hard' set to 0 when risk>tau. Add CLI flags --guard_mode, --alpha, --tau. Run baseline (off) vs soft vs hard on same tasks and budget; record private accuracy, total cost, #filtered nodes, avg risk, showing guard improves generalisation per dollar.

Name: diversity_bonus_search
Title: Diversity-Bonus Tree Search: Encouraging Novel Solutions in LLM-Powered ARC Solving
Experiment:
1) Add utils/diversity.py implementing
   - tokenize(code): split on non-alphanumerics, drop stopwords
   - jaccard(s1,s2) and code_similarity(c1,c2)
   - grid_similarity(g1,g2)=fraction_equal_cells; returns 1 when shapes differ
   - novelty_bonus(item, history, mode) where mode∈{'code','output'}; bonus = 1-max_similarity.
2) In experiment.py define global list code_history (and output_history if mode=='output'). After each GenerationResult, extract python code or first demo-output grid; compute bonus, then blended_score = (1-alpha)*public_score + alpha*bonus when --diversity_mode!='off'. Append the new representation to history. Public score itself is left untouched for logging.
3) Extend argparse with --diversity_mode {off,code,output} (default off) and --diversity_alpha FLOAT (default 0.3). Pass these via partial() to generate_fn.
4) Run StandardMCTS with diversity_mode='off' (baseline) and 'code' (α=0.3) on all tasks, 16 nodes each, recording private accuracy and number of distinct solutions (similarity<0.7).
5) Evaluate: Does diversity bonus yield higher private accuracy or more tasks solved within fixed budget? Analyse solved-per-dollar as secondary metric.

Name: self_evaluation_prior
Title: Leveraging LLM Self-Confidence as a Prior in Tree Search for ARC
Experiment: 1) Create utils/self_eval.py with build_self_eval_prompt(code, demos) that builds: 'Given the following Python function and paired examples, estimate probability (0-1) that the function will generalise to a new unseen input. Respond with only a number.' 2) In experiment.generate_fn(), after computing public score, assemble self-eval prompt and call call_llm(self_eval_model, 0.0, messages). Parse float c; if parse fails or c∉[0,1] set c=0.5. 3) Add argparse --self_eval_alpha (default 0) and --self_eval_model (default same nano model). 4) Compute blended_score = (1-alpha)*public_score + alpha*c; use blended_score for node.score, keep raw public_score for logging. 5) Run baseline alpha=0 and alpha in {0.3,0.5,0.7} over all tasks (16 nodes). Track private accuracy, total cost, solved-per-dollar. 6) Hypothesis: alpha≈0.5 yields higher hidden-set accuracy with <15% extra cost, demonstrating benefit of introspective priors.

Name: edit_action_mcts
Title: Incremental Code-Edit Actions for Efficient LLM Tree Search
Experiment: 1) Implement edit_prompt(parent_state, problem) that wraps BaselinePrompt.feedback_prompt and appends the instruction: 'Keep the previous code; apply minimal edits to fix the errors shown.' 2) Duplicate current generate_fn into generate_from_scratch (unchanged) and generate_edit which uses edit_prompt and a lower temperature (e.g. 0.3). 3) In main(), build generate_fns = {"scratch": generate_from_scratch, "edit": generate_edit}.  The tree algorithms can now branch on either action. 4) Book-keep cost/time per (action,model) pair. 5) Run StandardMCTS with 16 nodes on the ARC-AGI benchmark and compare to baseline single-action run.  Metrics: private accuracy, total cost, solved-per-dollar, average chain length of edits.  Hypothesis: allowing targeted edits yields more tasks solved and/or lower cost.

Name: prompt_ensemble_search
Title: Prompt Ensemble Thompson Sampling: Online Prompt Selection for LLM Tree Search
Experiment:
1) Implement 3 extra PromptTemplate subclasses (ShortPrompt, PatternPrompt, VisualPrompt) in prompts/; each tweaks wording and instructions but keeps the same IO format.
2) In experiment.py main(), build generate_fns = { 'baseline': partial(generate_fn, prompt_template=BaselinePrompt(...)), 'short': partial(generate_fn, prompt_template=ShortPrompt(...)), 'pattern': partial(generate_fn, prompt_template=PatternPrompt(...)), 'visual': partial(generate_fn, prompt_template=VisualPrompt(...)) }.  The dict keys become ACTION names.
3) Pass list(generate_fns.keys()) to ABMCTSAStateManager so NodeProbState tracks per-prompt reward; no other algorithm changes needed.  Each node expansion still triggers exactly one LLM call, so cost per node is unchanged.
4) Run the ARC-AGI benchmark with max_num_nodes=16 using StandardMCTS and AB-MCTS.  Compare to single-prompt baseline on: (a) private accuracy, (b) total cost, (c) solved-per-dollar, (d) per-task prompt selections for insight.
5) Expectation: adaptive prompt selection outperforms any single prompt and yields data on prompt-task affinity, demonstrating that prompt diversity is a valuable search dimension.

Name: learned_value_guidance
Title: Online Learned Value Function for Heuristic Guidance in LLM Tree Search
Experiment:
1) Add utils/value_model.py:
   - extract_features(node_state): code_token_count, ast_node_count, num_ifs, num_loops, avg_line_len, public_score.
   - ValueModel class using sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor with fit/predict.
2) In experiment.py define global buffers X_buffer, y_buffer and value_model.  For every new node store feats in X_buffer.  Once a node has at least lookahead_window descendants, compute y as the max public score among those descendants and append to y_buffer.
3) When len(y_buffer) >= min_samples and either len(y_buffer) is power of two or multiple of 100, call value_model.fit(X_buffer, y_buffer).  Persist model to disk.
4) Modify StandardMCTS._uct_score: before returning, compute value_pred = value_model.predict(feats) if model is trained else 0.5; then exploitation = (1-α)*exploitation + α*value_pred (CLI flag --value_alpha, default 0).
5) Add CLI flags --value_alpha, --lookahead_window, --value_update_min_samples.
6) Run baseline (alpha=0) and alpha in {0.3,0.6} on ARC-AGI (16 nodes).  Record private accuracy, solved-per-dollar, and correlation between value_pred and future rewards.
7) Expected: learned guidance increases hidden-set accuracy with <1% runtime overhead, demonstrating benefits of online surrogate learning.

Name: crossover_action
Title: Genetic Crossover Actions for Recombining Partial Programs in LLM Tree Search
Experiment: 1) Add generate_fn_crossover(state, task, prompt_template, model_name, model_temp, llm_log_dir, partner_selector) to experiment.py.   • Choose partner_state = partner_selector(search_tree) (default: highest-scoring node different from parent; optional CLI --crossover_topk to sample among top-k).   • Build prompt = BaselinePrompt.initial_prompt + two code blocks (parent and partner) + instruction: "Combine the strengths of both functions into a new `transform` that passes all demos; no hard-coding."   • Call call_llm and score as in generate_fn. 2) Build generate_fns = {"scratch": generate_fn (existing), "crossover": generate_fn_crossover}. 3) When creating NodeProbState (in ABMCTSAStateManager) include the new action name "crossover". 4) Optional argparse flags: --crossover_topk INT, --partner_strategy {best,random}. 5) Run baseline (scratch only) vs crossover-enabled search on ARC-AGI with identical node budgets (16). 6) Report: hidden-set accuracy, total cost, #tasks whose best solution descends from a crossover edge, and average improvement of crossover child over parents.  Success indicates recombination is a valuable primitive in program-synthesis-with-LLMs.

Name: global_codebank
Title: Global Codebank Memory: Knowledge Accumulation Across Tree Search for ARC
Experiment: 1) Add utils/codebank.py with class CodeBank(max_snippets=20, max_tokens=400, min_score=0.5).  Methods: add(code:str, score:float) parses code via ast and stores helper defs (name!=transform, length<=40 lines) with their score and token count; automatic FIFO or lowest-score eviction keeps total tokens<=max_tokens.  get_prompt_block() returns a string of concatenated snippets wrapped in <codebank> ... </codebank>. 2) In experiment.py create a task-local codebank instance at the start of main(); it lives for the duration of that task only. 3) Modify generate_fn(): (a) Prepend bank_block as a system message if not empty. (b) After scoring, if public_score>=min_score, call codebank.add(pycode, public_score). 4) Add CLI flags --codebank_on (bool), --codebank_max_snippets, --codebank_max_tokens, --codebank_threshold.  When off, behaviour matches baseline. 5) Extend time_summary.json with codebank_size, total_tokens, num_reuses (helper name appears in generated code). 6) Run StandardMCTS on ARC-AGI with identical node budget (16) in two settings: baseline and codebank_on.  Compare hidden-set accuracy, total cost, median prompt length, and reuse metrics.  Hypothesis: codebank yields >5% higher private accuracy with <10% cost increase.

Name: probe_action
Title: Interactive Probe Actions: Active Hypothesis Testing in LLM Tree Search for ARC
Experiment:
1) Implement generate_fn_probe(state, task, prompt_template, model_name, model_temp, llm_log_dir): build a prompt instructing the LLM to output ONE boolean function named `hypothesis` that receives (inp, out) and returns True/False; nothing else. Call call_llm, parse code, run on all demo pairs with try/except. Let p be fraction True. Score = (1 - |p-0.5|)  (highest when split) and set to 0 on crash.
2) Store probe results by inserting {'probe_truth': [bools]} into NodeState.eval_results so no new fields are required.
3) Extend BaselinePrompt.feedback_prompt: if action=='probe', append the probe code and the truth values per example so subsequent calls see verified facts.
4) Add new action entry to generate_fns and NodeProbState: {'transform': generate_fn, 'probe': generate_fn_probe}.  AB-MCTS can now choose between them automatically.
5) Optionally add --probe_weight CLI flag to scale probe reward relative to public score.
6) Run three settings (baseline, random probe ratio 0.5, AB-MCTS selection) on ARC-AGI with 16 nodes. Collect private accuracy, total cost, probes per task, and correlation between probe entropy and future score gains.
7) Expected outcome: probe-enabled search achieves ≥5% higher hidden-set accuracy with <20% additional cost, demonstrating that low-cost active queries can guide LLM program synthesis.

Name: cross_task_retrieval
Title: Cross-Task Retrieval and Adaptation for Continual LLM Tree Search on ARC
Experiment:
1) Add utils/solution_lib.py with: add_entry(task_id, signature, code, score); compute_signature(demos); similarity(sig1,sig2); get_topk(current_sig,k). Maintain a capped JSONL of top-N (e.g., 50) entries.
2) On task completion in main(), if best private score >= 0.9, compute signature(demos) and call add_entry.
3) Implement AdaptPrompt(PromptTemplate) that prepends up to k retrieved code snippets in a <reference_solutions> block before the usual task prompt.
4) Implement generate_fn_retrieve(...) that builds AdaptPrompt and registers action name "retrieve"; falls back to BaselinePrompt if library empty.
5) Build generate_fns = {"scratch": generate_fn, "retrieve": generate_fn_retrieve} and initialise NodeProbState with these actions so existing selection logic applies.
6) Run baseline vs retrieval-enabled (same 16-node budget) over ARC-AGI; log hidden-set accuracy, total cost, nodes-to-solve, and retrieval_hit_rate.

Name: auto_mutate
Title: Zero-Cost Program Mutation for Efficient LLM Tree Search on ARC
Experiment: 1) Add utils/mutation.py with function apply_random_mutation(code:str)->str.  Rules (pick one at random): (i) replace an int literal 0-9 with another; (ii) add/subtract 1 from an int; (iii) swap two indices in nested loops; (iv) toggle .copy() on a slice; (v) switch rows/cols in a shape expression.  Use ast, ensure the output still parses; on failure return None. 2) Implement generate_fn_mutate(state, task, ...): if state is None or code unavailable, return (state,0). Else mutate parent code, run task.generate_eval_results on demos, score = average demo accuracy, cost = 0.0; build new NodeState with model_name="mutation". 3) In experiment.py build generate_fns = {"transform": existing generate_fn, "mutate": generate_fn_mutate}. 4) When creating NodeProbState, pass actions=["transform","mutate"]. 5) Run StandardMCTS & AB-MCTS with 16 nodes on ARC-AGI benchmark.  Report: private accuracy, total LLM cost, solved-per-dollar, and fraction of best solutions obtained via mutation.  Expect mutation to fix simple bugs at zero cost, boosting hidden-set accuracy within the same budget.

Name: dense_reward_shaping
Title: Dense Reward Shaping for Efficient LLM Tree Search on ARC
Experiment:
1) Add utils/grid_metrics.py with:
   - pixel_accuracy(pred,gold) = mean(pred==gold)
   - palette_overlap(pred,gold) = |palette∩|/|palette∪|, where palette is set(unique colours).
   - dense_score(pred,gold,w1=0.7,w2=0.3) = w1*pixel_accuracy + w2*palette_overlap.
2) Modify experiment.generate_fn(): after eval_results and public_score, compute dense_reward = average_{demo}(dense_score).  Blend: blended = (1-dense_alpha)*public_score + dense_alpha*dense_reward (CLI flag --dense_alpha, default 0.5).  Use blended for node.score; keep public_score for logging.
3) Optional: if --dense_feedback True, append per-example dense metrics to feedback_prompt so LLM sees partial correctness.
4) Add argparse flags: --dense_alpha FLOAT, --dense_feedback BOOL.
5) Run baseline (dense_alpha=0) and shaped variants (0.5, 0.8) with StandardMCTS on ARC-AGI (16 nodes).  Record hidden-set accuracy, nodes-to-first-perfect, total cost, solved-per-dollar.
6) Expectation: shaped reward guides search to good programs faster, improving accuracy under same budget.

Name: multi_completion_branching
Title: Branch Once, Explore Many: Exploiting Multi-Completion LLM Calls for Efficient Tree Search
Experiment: 1) Extend utils/llm_builder.call_llm(model, temp, messages, n_completions=1) -> (list[str] generations, float total_cost). If backend lacks native multi-complete, loop internally. 2) Add class BufferedGenerator(partial_params, k) that internally stores extra (state,score) pairs. When empty it calls call_llm with n_completions=k, scores each generation, enqueues them, and returns one. 3) Modify experiment.generate_fn to support k>1 and cost splitting: each node is assigned total_cost/k. 4) In experiment.py create generate_fns using BufferedGenerator with k=args.k_per_call (CLI flag, default 1). No changes to tree algorithms. 5) Optional flag --adaptive_k to reduce k if runtime per call grows too high. 6) Compare baseline (k=1) with k=3 on ARC-AGI (16 nodes) measuring private accuracy, total cost, cost-per-solve, and wall-clock time. Expect multi-completion to raise accuracy or cut cost with minimal implementation effort.

Name: llm_meta_select
Title: LLM-Guided Meta-Selection for Node Expansion in Tree Search
Experiment: 1) Create utils/llm_controller.py with:   (a) summarise_node(node) -> str that returns f"score={node.score:.2f}, depth={node.depth}, snippet={first 10 lines of code with ellipsis}".   (b) llm_pick_node(candidates, model="gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14", temp=0.0) that builds a prompt: 'Below are N candidate partial solutions. Choose the idx that is most promising. Respond with only the integer.'  Calls call_llm, parses int; on failure returns candidates[0]. 2) Subclass StandardMCTS as LLMGuidedMCTS overriding _select: compute standard UCT on leaves, keep top_k (flag --selection_topk, default 8), build candidate list [{'idx':id, 'desc':summarise_node(node)}], call llm_pick_node when flag --llm_meta_select is True and tree has ≥top_k leaves, otherwise fall back to original _select. 3) Add CLI flags --llm_meta_select BOOL and --selection_topk INT. 4) In experiment.py set algorithm = LLMGuidedMCTS() when flag true. 5) Run ARC-AGI twice: baseline StandardMCTS vs LLMGuidedMCTS with identical max_num_nodes (16).  Log hidden-set accuracy, total LLM cost, number of guidance calls, and percentage of times the chosen node was not the max-UCT node but led to higher eventual score. 6) Hypothesis: meta-selection improves solved-per-dollar by leveraging LLM semantic judgement at negligible extra cost.

Name: adaptive_temperature_bandit
Title: Creativity Scheduling: Adaptive Temperature Selection via Bandit Strategies in LLM Tree Search
Experiment:
1) Define TEMPS = [0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0] in experiment.py main().
2) For each temperature t create generate_fns entry: key=f"temp_{t}", value=partial(generate_fn, model_name="gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14", model_temp=t, prompt_template=BaselinePrompt(...)). All arms have identical cost.
3) Initialise ABMCTSAStateManager with actions=list(generate_fns.keys()) and model_selection_strategy="multiarm_bandit_thompson" (already supported).
4) Depth-aware prior (optional): when NodeProbState is created, set reward_average_prior = 0.7 for depth 0, linearly cooling to 0.3 by depth 4+, via PriorConfig.set_reward_average_prior().
5) Run two settings on the full ARC-AGI benchmark with max_num_nodes=16: (A) baseline fixed temp 0.6 (current code), (B) adaptive_temperature_bandit.
6) Log per-iteration chosen temperature, best private score, and total cost. Analyse (i) hidden-set accuracy, (ii) tasks solved first by each temperature, (iii) entropy/cooling of temp selections, and (iv) solved-per-dollar improvement.

Name: self_consistency_bonus
Title: Self-Consistency Checks via Synthetic Examples Improve Generalisation in LLM Tree Search
Experiment:
1) Add utils/self_consistency.py implementing:
   - build_messages(demos) -> messages requesting ONE additional input/output pair in JSON format.
   - parse_pair(gen) -> (input_grid, output_grid) or None.
   - pixel_accuracy(g1,g2).
2) In experiment.generate_fn(): after public_score is computed, if --self_consistency_on:
   a) Call call_llm(self_consistency_model, 0.0, build_messages(...)).
   b) Parse pair; run newly produced transform on synthetic input.
   c) consistency = pixel_accuracy(pred, claimed_out) (0 if parse/exec fails).
   d) node_score = (1-alpha)*public_score + alpha*consistency, alpha from --self_consistency_alpha (default 0.5).
   e) Store {'synthetic_io': (inp,out), 'consistency': consistency} in NodeState; log both scores.
3) Modify BaselinePrompt.feedback_prompt to display the synthetic example and whether the model passed.
4) CLI flags: --self_consistency_on (bool, default true), --self_consistency_alpha FLOAT, --self_consistency_model (default cheap model name).
5) Run ablation: baseline (flag off) vs self-consistency (flag on, alpha=0.5) on ARC-AGI with 16 nodes; report hidden-set accuracy, total cost, and correlation between consistency and private score.

Name: hierarchical_plan_execute
Title: Hierarchical Plan-Execute Tree Search: Separating Reasoning and Coding in LLM-Powered ARC Solving
Experiment:
1) Add PlanPrompt(PromptTemplate) that asks the LLM to output ONLY a high-level plan in <plan></plan> tags followed by a confidence number in <score></score> (0-1).
2) Add optional field plan_text to NodeState; if not None the node represents a plan.
3) Implement generate_fn_plan(state, ...): build prompt with PlanPrompt (initial or feedback), call LLM (nano model, temp 0.3, low max_tokens).  Parse <score>; fallback 0.5.  Return NodeState(plan_text, score, model_name).
4) Implement generate_fn_execute(parent_state, ...): if parent_state.plan_text exists, build prompt: 'Here is a PLAN:\n<plan>...</plan>\nImplement it as the transform function.'  Call LLM (temp 0.6), evaluate on demos, score = mean accuracy.  If no plan_text, fall back to baseline transform generation.
5) Extend generate_fns = {"plan": generate_fn_plan, "execute": generate_fn_execute}; initialise NodeProbState with these two actions so AB-MCTS can pick cheaply between them.
6) Run ARC-AGI with max_num_nodes=16 comparing baseline vs hierarchical_plan_execute.  Record hidden-set accuracy, total cost, action distribution, and solves-per-dollar.
